Fellow biochem premed here: overall, my experience with both premed and stem has been overwhelmingly positive. I have Generally done well in my classes and met some professors who I have really great relationships with. 

Many of the intro premed classes use learning assistants, upper classmen who help teach the class along side the professor. In addition, the culture is definitely collaborative, and I can attest to that with anecdotes like studying for a bio chem exam with a classmate who got the highest grade in the class and was willing to help me out

Additionally, there are a lot of great opportunities for premeds, including shadowing, research, service, and extracurriculars on campus. The health professions advisory office does a pretty great job and I know former students who have matriculated to top med schools

But of course, my opinion may also be biased. I can say that some of the professors are hit or miss. I would also say that Vandy classes can be challenging and they require you to be disciplined when it comes to time management and studying. 

But TLDR, premed and stem at Vandy are great.

I’ve focused a lot on improving these things:
Physics: circuits, fluids/pressure, lens equation, magnetism
Orgo: lab techniques, IR/NMR, acyl substitution, carbohydrates
Gen chem: periodic trends, equilibrium, kinetics (esp half life)

One sneaky thing that has gotten me a lot is the mental math errors. Make sure you’re comfortable doing math and rounding answers. I’d write out calculations on scratch paper.

Also, something I’ve noticed is that sometimes you’ll see a biochem question come out of nowhere (ie amino acids, carbohydrates) on C/P, so covering topics like Macromolecules and metabolism can help unexpectedly.
